_doc: PRE-REGISTERED design for the MEASURED-MOVE study (base-depth -> projected target). Frozen BEFORE any depth/MFE/touch computation or exit replay is run (ground rule: exploratory != confirmatory -- no re-picks after seeing results; a NULL result is fully publishable). Motivated by 2026-07-09: J read an inverse head-and-shoulders on SPY (neckline 747.5, head 743.3, projection = neckline + (neckline-head) ~= 751.7) and price hit it; the engine traded the neckline reclaim (level_reclaim trigger) but has no concept of a projected target from base depth. QUESTION: does base-depth-derived projection carry real information (Question A), and would a projected-target runner exit beat trail-only (Question B)? NEITHER of today's actual signals is in either signal-set window used here (burned ends 2026-06-18, fresh ends 2026-07-08) -- the motivating trade is NOT itself in-sample anywhere in this study, avoiding the exact circularity structure_stop_study.py flagged for its own motivating example.

scope_interpretation.statement: 'the ribbon_ride level-reclaim population' is read as the LEVEL-TRIGGERED ribbon_ride population -- BOTH directions (BULLISH_RECLAIM_RIDE_THE_RIBBON via detect_level_reclaim, side C, AND BEARISH_REJECTION_RIDE_THE_RIBBON via detect_level_rejection, side P) -- not calls-only. Two pieces of evidence support this reading over a calls-only literal parse: (1) the task's own depth/projection formula is given as 'calls; mirrored for puts', which would be vacuous documentation if puts were out of scope; (2) structure_stop_study.py (the tool this study is instructed to reuse) is explicitly scoped to 'ribbon_ride (both directions)', and this study reuses its loaders/replay verbatim. Disclosed as a judgment call, not silently assumed.
scope_interpretation.today_example_role: The 747.5-neckline/743.3-head trade that motivated this study occurred 2026-07-09, AFTER both signal-set windows end (burned <= 2026-06-18, fresh <= 2026-07-08) -- it is illustrative only, never a data point in this study.

exploratory_burned.sha256_note: sha256 of the RAW FILE BYTES (t5_confirmatory_matrix.py's EXPECTED_SHA16 convention) -- re-verified by hand before freezing this file: MATCH.
exploratory_burned.label_rationale: Consumed by T3/T4/T5's exploratory grids already -- 'burned' (seen), included here for statistical power and as the non-decisive corroboration layer, not the decision-maker.

fresh_decisive.sha256_note: sha256 of json.dumps(sort_keys=True) of the KEPT signals list only (structure_stop_study.py's EXPECTED_FRESH_SHA16 convention) -- re-verified by hand before freezing this file: MATCH.
fresh_decisive.label_rationale: Never seen by any exploratory grid -- the DECISIVE layer per the task's own framing ('fresh slice = decisive').

trigger_level_recovery.method: tw8_level_context's PUBLIC functions called directly (frozen_level_set_for_date + find_trigger_bar + lib.filters.detect_level_reclaim/detect_level_rejection) -- the IDENTICAL method tw8_level_context.enrich_signal uses internally, called directly (not via enrich_signal) because this study additionally needs the trigger BAR's own timestamp (for the K-bar depth window), which enrich_signal's return value does not expose. tw8_level_context.py is NOT edited (ANALYSIS ONLY / no live-file-edits constraint) -- this is a new, additive caller of its existing public surface.
trigger_level_recovery.spy_history_window: 2025-01-01..2026-07-08 (covers both signal-set windows exactly; verified locally cached as backtest/data/spy_5m_2025-01-01_2026-07-08.csv before freezing this file)

empirically_observed_at_freeze_time.note: Recorded here for pre-registration transparency (verified by hand before freezing) -- NOT a re-pick trigger. The population size is a property of the existing signal sets + the existing level detector, not a parameter this study tunes.

trigger_level_recovery.fallback_rule_question_a: A signal without a recoverable trigger_level has no depth/projection and is EXCLUDED from Question A (the information test) by construction -- disclosed exclusion, not a biased drop (there is nothing to measure).
trigger_level_recovery.fallback_rule_question_b: A signal without a recoverable trigger_level is NEVER dropped from Question B -- under the PROJECTION_ONLY / PROJECTION_OR_TRAIL policies it is replayed with the projection-touch check inert (degrading EXACTLY to the TRAIL_ONLY control's own byte-identical replay logic for that signal). This is a conservative fallback: it can only pull a challenger's aggregate toward control, never away from it in the challenger's favor.

base_depth_definition.formula_calls: depth = trigger_level - min(low) over the K SPY 5-min bars strictly preceding the trigger bar (timestamp_et < trigger_bar_time, taking the LAST K such bars chronologically). projection = trigger_level + depth.
base_depth_definition.formula_puts_mirrored: depth = max(high over the same K-bar window) - trigger_level. projection = trigger_level - depth.
base_depth_definition.window_convention: Bar-count based across the continuous 5-min SPY sequence, NOT session-bounded -- an early-morning trigger bar may pull bars from the prior trading session to reach K bars. All bars used satisfy timestamp_et < trigger_bar_time (strict), preserving C6 (no look-ahead: the trigger bar itself and everything after it is excluded from the depth measurement).
base_depth_definition.k_grid_rationale: 5-min bars: K=12 ~= 1h base, K=24 ~= 2h base, K=48 ~= 4h base. K=24 is PRIMARY (frozen decision point for the touch-rate/tercile table and the shuffle null); K=12/K=48 are SENSITIVITY ONLY, reported but never decision-driving.
base_depth_definition.negative_depth_floor: A raw (trigger_level - min(low)) [calls] or (max(high) - trigger_level) [puts] can be marginally negative when the K-bar window does not fully capture the pattern's true extreme (e.g. the extreme printed just before the window's own start). Such values are CLIPPED to 0.0 and counted separately (depth_K{K}_clipped flag + n_depth_clipped aggregate) -- never silently kept negative (a negative 'base depth' is not interpretable) and never dropped.
base_depth_definition.short_window_handling: If fewer than K prior bars exist at all (data-start edge case), depth is computed from whatever bars ARE available (n_bars_used < K, disclosed) unless ZERO prior bars exist (spy_full has no bars before the trigger bar), in which case depth/projection = None for that signal (falls back exactly like an unrecoverable trigger_level). Empirically observed at freeze time: n_short_window = 0 for all three K values on this population (no data-start edge cases are actually hit).

position_horizon_and_outcomes.horizon_start: entry_ts (the signal's own tradeable entry bar -- one bar after the trigger bar per tw8_level_context's documented ENTRY_TS-vs-ENTRY_SPOT convention).
position_horizon_and_outcomes.horizon_end: the EARLIEST of: (a) the structure-stop fire time -- structure_stop_study.structure_stop_signal_time(spy_lifetime, side, trigger_level, buffer=0.0), reused VERBATIM (same C6-safe closed-5m-bar-close, next-bar-open-of-breach convention already validated in structure_stop_study.py's own test suite); (b) 15:40 ET same day (t4_exit_matrix.py / t5_confirmatory_matrix.py TIME_STOP convention, the SAME time-stop this study's own Question B replay uses); (c) the last available SPY bar of that trading day.
position_horizon_and_outcomes.rationale: Ties 'position horizon' directly to the SAME chart-stop-primary structure-stop mechanism (v15.3 doctrine) already governing this exact signal population -- this is not an arbitrary new invalidation rule, it is the one the live/backtest engine already applies.
position_horizon_and_outcomes.mfe_definition: MFE (calls) = max(high over [entry_ts, horizon_end]) - trigger_level. MFE (puts) = trigger_level - min(low over the same window). Reference basis is trigger_level (the SAME anchor depth/projection use), not the option entry premium -- keeps depth/projection/MFE on one consistent SPY-price basis. Reported signed (not floored at 0); a negative MFE means price never traded back to trigger_level at all before horizon_end.
position_horizon_and_outcomes.touch_definition: touched_projection (calls) = max(high over the horizon window) >= projection, equivalently MFE >= depth. touched_projection (puts) = min(low over the horizon window) <= projection, equivalently MFE >= depth. By construction 'touched before stopping' is automatically satisfied: the horizon window already ends at the structure-stop fire time when one occurs, so any touch counted is provably prior to that stop.
position_horizon_and_outcomes.time_to_touch_definition: For touched signals only: (first bar's timestamp within the horizon window whose high/low satisfies the touch condition) - entry_ts, in minutes. None for un-touched signals.

question_a_information_test.population: all signals with a recoverable trigger_level (n=112 at freeze time) AND a non-empty horizon outcome (outcome_status=='ok').
question_a_information_test.primary_statistic: tercile touch-rate spread: touch_rate(deepest depth_K24 tercile) - touch_rate(shallowest depth_K24 tercile), pooled across both windows. One-sided (directional hypothesis: deeper base -> higher touch rate).
question_a_information_test.secondary_statistic: Spearman rank correlation between depth_K24 and MFE, pooled across both windows. Two-sided.
question_a_information_test.tercile_method: Sort the eligible population by depth_K24 ascending; split into 3 groups of nearly-equal size (remainder bars distributed to the first groups). Report per tercile: n, depth range, touch_rate, median_time_to_touch_min (touched signals only), mean_mfe, median_mfe.
question_a_information_test.reporting_table: By depth tercile: touch rate, median time-to-touch, MFE (mean + median) -- exactly the table the task requests.
question_a_information_test.sensitivity: The SAME tercile table + Spearman correlation, recomputed for K=12 and K=48, reported alongside K=24 as sensitivity checks (not decision-driving).
question_a_information_test.fresh_slice_only_view: A SEPARATE, SMALL-BY-CONSTRUCTION (n=14 recoverable of 18) tercile table restricted to fresh_decisive signals only, reported for descriptive/informational purposes. NO separate shuffle null is run on this subset (underpowered at n=14 for a 3-way split) -- it is context, not a second decision layer.

shuffle_null.method: Permute the depth_K24 VALUES across the pooled eligible population (n=112) while holding each signal's own MFE/touched_projection outcome fixed -- i.e. randomly reassign which signal 'owns' which depth value, recompute BOTH the primary and secondary statistics on the shuffled assignment. Repeat N_PERM=2000 times with a fixed deterministic seed (PERM_SEED=1337, python's stdlib random.Random -- reproducible across runs, no global RNG side effects, matching autoresearch.null_baseline.py's determinism convention).
shuffle_null.reporting: For each statistic: the REAL value, the null distribution's mean + std (non-vacuity requires std > 0), the empirical p-value (one-sided for the tercile spread: fraction of null values >= real; two-sided for Spearman: fraction of |null| >= |real|), and the real value's percentile rank within the null distribution.
shuffle_null.interpretation_note: This is an INFORMATION test, not a ship/kill gate -- Question A has no pass bar. A conventional p<0.05 read is offered as calibration only, not as a hard threshold.

shared_body_SS_B.source: structure_stop_study.SS_B_SHAPE, reused VERBATIM: premium_stop_pct=-0.50 (catastrophe cap), tp1_premium_pct=1.0 (TP1 at +100%), tp1_qty_fraction=0.667 (sell66), PLUS the structure-stop-primary layer (structure_stop_study.structure_stop_signal_time, buffer=0.0, side-aware) sitting in front of plan_exit_actions -- the EXACT SS-B candidate the referenced structure-stop study already validated as the live cell. This study changes ONLY the post-TP1 runner policy; the pre-TP1 body (structure stop / catastrophe cap / TP1) is IDENTICAL across all three candidates.
shared_body_SS_B.qty: t4_exit_matrix.QTY = 10 (fixed), matching every prior anchor/exploratory tool in this line -- tp1_qty=int(10*0.667)=6, runner_qty=4.
shared_body_SS_B.time_stop: 15:40 ET (t4/t5 TIME_STOP convention) for BOTH windows -- matches how signal-set.json and the fresh slice are already consumed identically elsewhere in this codebase.

i_TRAIL_ONLY.label: trail15 only (the live SS-B cell) -- CONTROL
i_TRAIL_ONLY.definition: profit_lock_mode='trailing', trail_pct=0.15 -- SS_B_SHAPE completely unmodified. This is a parity-verified byte-identical replay of structure_stop_study.replay_structure_aware under SS_B_SHAPE (see test_measured_move_study.py).

ii_PROJECTION_ONLY.label: exit runner at the projection
ii_PROJECTION_ONLY.definition: Post-TP1, profit_lock_mode is set to 'fixed' (BE floor only, no trailing) AND a new projection-touch check is added: once the runner phase begins (state.tp1_filled==True), if the SPY bar aligned (by time-of-day, via tw8_level_context.spy_bars_by_time_for_day -- the SAME alignment convention documented for 'candidate R's retest scan') to the current option bar shows high>=projection (calls) / low<=projection (puts), SELL_ALL the runner at THAT option bar's CLOSE.
ii_PROJECTION_ONLY.fill_convention: Option bar CLOSE at the matching SPY-bar timestamp -- the SAME 'known-in-time market exit' fill convention already used for time-stop/EOD-mark fills throughout t4_exit_matrix.py and structure_stop_study.py (there is no formula translating a SPY price level into an option premium without Black-Scholes, which this codebase avoids per the real-fills doctrine).
ii_PROJECTION_ONLY.fallback: If this signal has no recoverable trigger_level (projection is None), the shape is NOT modified to 'fixed' -- it stays 'trailing' (SS_B_SHAPE unmodified), i.e. this signal's replay is byte-identical to TRAIL_ONLY. Verified by test.

iii_PROJECTION_OR_TRAIL.label: projection-OR-trail whichever first
iii_PROJECTION_OR_TRAIL.definition: Post-TP1, profit_lock_mode STAYS 'trailing' (trail_pct=0.15, unchanged from control) AND the SAME projection-touch check from (ii) runs concurrently. Whichever fires first (by bar) closes the runner.
iii_PROJECTION_OR_TRAIL.fallback: If projection is None for this signal, the projection-touch branch is simply always-false -- replay is byte-identical to TRAIL_ONLY for that signal.

runner_policies.same_bar_tie_break: STOP-FIRST -- if, within the SAME 5-min bar, both plan_exit_actions' own runner-exit action (trail-stop / BE-stop / time-stop) AND the projection-touch condition would fire, the ordinary plan_exit_actions action wins (checked first; the projection check is skipped that bar). This is t4_exit_matrix.py's OWN documented convention ('Same-bar -S/+T ties resolve STOP-FIRST'), applied uniformly here rather than invented ad hoc.

question_b_exit_test.metrics: t4_exit_matrix.battery(trades) reused verbatim per (policy, window) -- gives n/total/expectancy/wr/exp_drop_top3/oos/wf/qpf/worst_trade/max_dd -- PLUS a per-band breakdown (t4_exit_matrix.band_of/BANDS) and n_used_projection / n_fallback_to_trail (L176 discipline: confirm the projection mechanism actually fires on a meaningful fraction of trades before trusting any sweep of it).

pass_bar.statement: A challenger (ii or iii) PASSES only if ALL FOUR conditions hold (frozen, no partial credit):
pass_bar.condition_1: expectancy on fresh_decisive STRICTLY GREATER THAN control's expectancy on fresh_decisive.
pass_bar.condition_2: expectancy on exploratory_burned STRICTLY GREATER THAN control's expectancy on exploratory_burned.
pass_bar.condition_3: exp_drop_top3 (expectancy after removing the 3 largest winners) POSITIVE (>0) on fresh_decisive.
pass_bar.beats_definition: STRICTLY GREATER THAN -- a tie is not a beat (structure_stop_study.py's established convention).
pass_bar.outcome_if_no_challenger_passes: CONTROL (trail-only) STANDS -- explicit, matches the task's own framing.
pass_bar.outcome_if_a_challenger_passes: That challenger is PROPOSED (not auto-shipped -- this study is ANALYSIS ONLY, report-only, no wiring per the task's own closing instruction).

cautions_baked_in_from_doctrine: C30 (exit-target knobs are repeatedly dead/harmful here, L148/L176/L177/L178): Question B reports n_used_projection / n_fallback_to_trail AND n_projection_fired per policy per window -- if the projection-touch mechanism rarely or never actually fires (a near-dead knob), that is reported prominently, not buried, regardless of the aggregate expectancy delta.

C27 (pattern detectors firing on >80% of days measure noise, L145): if Question A's touch rate is uniformly high across ALL terciles (including the shallowest), that is evidence the projection is trivially reached regardless of depth (noise, not signal) -- the shuffle null is the primary defense against over-reading a high-but-undiscriminating touch rate as 'depth matters'.

C6 (no look-ahead): depth uses ONLY bars strictly before the trigger bar; MFE/touch/horizon use ONLY bars from entry_ts through horizon_end (which itself is bounded by the C6-safe structure-stop convention). Tested explicitly (test_measured_move_study.py) with a planted look-ahead bar that would materially change the result if leaked.
A NULL result on either question is fully publishable -- no re-picks, no scope changes, no new K values or policies added after this file is frozen.
no_repick_clause: Once this file is frozen, no K value, horizon rule, depth formula, fill convention, tie-break rule, or pass-bar condition may be edited in light of results. A NULL/FAIL is a publishable, informative outcome, not a reason to adjust the pre-registration and re-run.

closed_2026_09_02.verdict: KILL on both questions. Question A (does base depth carry information about the projected target?): n_eligible=111, shuffle-null spread p=0.998, Spearman p=0.1155 -- indistinguishable from shuffled. Question B (does a measured-move target beat the incumbent exit?): CONTROL_TRAIL_ONLY_STANDS. The projection carries no information AND does not beat trail-only.
closed_2026_09_02.note: Populations disclosed as designed: 250 exploratory_burned (98 recoverable trigger_level, 152 fallback) and 18 fresh_decisive (14 recoverable). The verdict rests on the information test, which does not depend on the fallback split.
